implementation_notes: Swift's blob is usually the observable object behind SwiftUI's `@EnvironmentObject`, or a view model that accumulates state for several screens — a class with `user`, `cart`, `settings`, `theme` and `notifications` where each method touches a different subset. The detection is easy (property references per method) and the split is per-feature observable objects with explicit injection, which is the design SwiftUI already offers. The Swift-specific reason the blob is easy to write is that `@EnvironmentObject` injects one object into the entire view tree, so no view's initialiser has to declare what it uses.
idiom_name: one view model holding every screen's state
pitfalls: `@EnvironmentObject` hides the dependency from every initialiser, so nothing in the view tree records which fields it uses.
Splitting into several observable objects multiplies the injection points and the invalidation work, which is a real cost and the reason the blob is often left in place.
A `static let shared` accumulating state is the same blob plus a singleton.
